sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Grid-Tie Solar Inverters and Microinverters

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL formation and governance), and R.223-1 et seq. (registration procedures)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) within the jurisdiction of the registered office; filings via the Guichet Unique (INPI online portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) executed by all shareholders, accompanied by the M0 form (déclaration de création d'entreprise) and supporting annexes
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; however, cash contributions must be fully paid up at subscription or at least 20% paid up at incorporation (balance within 5 years). Capital must be deposited in a blocked escrow account with a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts until registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the shareholders, having subscribed to the entire share capital of the SARL, hereby adopt the Statuts as filed. RESOLVED: That the registered office is fixed at [address], France. RESOLVED: That [Name] is appointed as Gérant (Manager) for an indefinite term with full powers to act on behalf of the company, including opening bank accounts, signing contracts, and representing the company before all authorities. RESOLVED: That the Gérant is authorized to complete all formalities for registration, publication, and licensing. RESOLVED: That the initial capital deposit be released from escrow upon issuance of the K-bis certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) – online database; no formal reservation required but recommended
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a search on the INPI database to ensure the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing trademarks or corporate names. Optionally file a declaration of name reservation with the Greffe du Commerce (fee ~€15) to secure the name for 8 weeks.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of the applicant
Power of attorney if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is rejected or conflicting, submit a new name or file an opposition response with the INPI within 2 months; otherwise, select an alternative name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Statuts (Articles of Association)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional but recommended for real estate contributions) or any signatory; legal counsel for drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts in French, including corporate purpose (manufacture of grid-tie solar inverters and microinverters), share capital, share classes, management structure (Gérant), and governance rules. All shareholders must sign the Statuts, either in private writing (sous seing privé) or by notarial deed if real property is contributed. Each shareholder must initial each page and sign the final page.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of capital deposit (if already made)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the Statuts for missing clauses or legal errors, amend the document and re-execute with all parties; notarization may be required if the registry insists.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account in the company's name (or in the name of the future company) and deposit the cash capital. Obtain a certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds) from the bank. The funds remain blocked until the company is registered and the certificate of registration (K-bis) is issued.
required_dossiers: Proof of address of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the deposit due to incomplete documentation, provide the missing documents or choose another bank. If the deposit is delayed, extend the timeline and notify the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Legal Notice in a Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a notice of incorporation in a legal gazette (JAL) containing the company name, form (SARL), capital, registered office, corporate purpose, and duration. Obtain a certificate of publication (attestation de parution) from the gazette.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette rejects the notice due to incomplete information, correct the text and republish. Ensure the notice is published within 1 week of signing the Statuts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Greffe du Commerce (Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Commerce (via Guichet Unique at guichet-entreprises.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation file electronically through the Guichet Unique portal. The file includes the M0 form, signed Statuts, certificate of capital deposit, publication attestation, and identity documents of the Gérant. Pay the filing fee (approx. €45). The registry reviews the file and issues the K-bis certificate (extract of registration) within 4-5 business days.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office address (lease or utility bill)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query (demande de complément), respond within 15 days with the requested documents. If the file is rejected, correct the errors and resubmit. If the K-bis is delayed, contact the registry or escalate to the supervising judge (juge commis à la surveillance du registre).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Formalities and Release of Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the K-bis certificate, the company is legally formed. Release the escrowed capital by providing the bank with the K-bis. Register for social security (URSSAF), tax (SIRET number), and obtain a VAT number (if applicable). Publish the incorporation in the BODACC (Bulletin Officiel des Annonces Civiles et Commerciales) automatically via the registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank does not release funds, provide the K-bis and a formal request. If SIRET is not issued, contact the Greffe to verify the registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS) – for industrial operations and workplace compliance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'exploitation (Operating Permit) under the French Environmental Code (Code de l'environnement) – specifically ICPE (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement) authorization or declaration, depending on activity thresholds

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique – Direction Générale de la Prévention des Risques (DGPR) and regional DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (Declaration) – for low-impact manufacturing of electronic components, subject to registration (déclaration) under ICPE if the facility exceeds certain thresholds (e.g., surface area > 200 m² or use of hazardous substances). A full EIA is not required for this activity unless the facility is located in a sensitive zone or exceeds 1,000 m².
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with French and EU standards: wastewater discharge limits per ICPE order (e.g., pH 5.5-8.5, COD < 125 mg/L, TSS < 35 mg/L); VOC emissions per Directive 2010/75/EU (Industrial Emissions Directive) – limit of 50 mg C/m³ for solvent-based processes; waste handling per Code de l'environnement (Articles R.541-1 et seq.) – mandatory waste tracking and disposal via licensed contractors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local fire department (Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours – SDIS) for premises > 300 m²; structural load inspection by a certified engineer (Bureau de Contrôle) to ensure floor load capacity for heavy equipment; workplace clearance (permis de travail) from the DREETS for compliance with the Labor Code (Code du travail) – including electrical safety, emergency exits, and ergonomic standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); day-to-day corporate and VAT compliance handled by the territorial Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); large international groups file with the Direction des Grandes Entreprises (DGE); non-resident businesses use the DGFiP non-resident department. Primary portals: impots.gouv.fr (filing, TIN status, VIES, OSS/IOSS access), formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (single registration window), and douane.gouv.fr (DELTA export declarations).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1 — Incorporate the SARL through the mandatory Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, submitting certified articles of association, proof of registered office lease, appointment of the gérant (manager), directors' identification and the beneficial-owner declaration (RBE). INSEE then issues the 9-digit SIREN and 14-digit SIRET, and the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce records the company in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés. STEP 2 — DGFiP automatically opens a fiscal dossier and transmits the intra-Community VAT number (format: FR + two-digit key + 9-digit SIREN), together with the corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés) account reference and a payment account for the SIE. VIES verification is available after issuance. STEP 3 — For a non-resident parent establishing a French fixed establishment rather than a French SARL, the same Guichet Unique or, where no French entity is incorporated, the DGFiP non-resident registration route (including the declaration d'existence form 1442-SD) is used to obtain a SIREN and French VAT number; the EU One-Stop-Shop is only available for distance sales of goods/imports and does not replace full VAT registration for French warehousing, manufacturing or export operations. STEP 4 — File the first or periodic VAT return (CA3) with the SIE and retain the French VAT ID before claiming any 0% export treatment. Total typical issuance time: 2-4 weeks from incorporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a standard commercial SARL is taxable as a separate legal person on Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) and is not pass-through. France additionally applies the territoriality principle under Article 209-I CGI: profits of the French business establishment are taxed in France, while profits attributable to a genuine foreign permanent establishment may be exempt; no tax-exempt zone status applies to an ordinary metropolitan France SARL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no check-the-box election. Available statutory mechanisms include: (1) fiscal integration election under Article 223-A CGI for a 95%+ French group, consolidating IS results; (2) VAT group election under Article 256-C CGI allowing jointly-controlled group members to form a single taxable person; (3) for qualifying small companies, the reduced 15% IS rate on the first EUR 42,500 of annual profit (requiring revenue below EUR 10 million, applied via the tax return election); (4) election for the simplified real tax accounting regime (régime simplifié d'imposition) below the statutory turnover ceiling; (5) optional 3-year IS exoneration for new qualifying businesses in assisted areas under Article 44-sexies CGI; (6) the authorization-based 'bénéfice mondial ou consolidé' election under Article 209-quinquies CGI to switch from territoriality to worldwide taxation; and (7) mandatory — not elective — application of the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive hybrid-mismatch rules and the OECD Pillar Two GloBE top-up tax (QDMTT/IIR) for groups above EUR 750 million. Ordinary SARLs do not qualify for the 'SARL de famille' personal income tax option unless the shareholders are family members, which is not available to a foreign-controlled SARL acting as an exporter/manufacturer.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA) under Articles 256-289-bis of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI) and Directive 2006/112/EC; no sales-and-use tax; import VAT is collected at customs clearance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 10,000 for intra-EU distance sales of goods where the OSS threshold applies; for B2B manufacturers and exporters there is no threshold — VAT registration is compulsory from the first taxable transaction under Article 286 CGI. The domestic 'franchise en base' exemption (Article 293-B CGI: EUR 85,000 for goods, EUR 25,000 for services) does not benefit an exporting SARL that must recover input VAT on components, machinery and logistics, and export sales must be declared with zero-rating entitlements through a full VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates structured electronic invoicing under Ordonnance n°2022-1473 and Article 289-bis CGI. Phased application: from 1 September 2026 all businesses must be able to receive e-invoices and large/medium enterprises (grandes entreprises and ETI) must issue them; from 1 September 2027 all small and micro enterprises must issue. Invoices must transit through an accredited Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP) or the Public Invoicing Portal (PPF) using structured formats compliant with EN 16931 (Factur-X, UBL, CII or EDI); cross-border exports and B2C transactions are covered by e-reporting of line-level transaction and payment data to DGFiP. The French model is continuous transmission to the tax administration with platform acknowledgement, not real-time tax-authority pre-clearance or digital stamping of each invoice; penalties for non-compliant e-invoicing apply from the enforcement dates under Article 1737 CGI (per-invoice fines and refusal of deduction).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exonération avec droit à déduction) is available for: (1) exports of tangible goods leaving France for a destination outside the European Union under Article 262-I-1° CGI, including shipments to French overseas departments treated as outside the EU fiscal territory; the goods must be dispatched by the seller, the buyer or on their behalf, and the exporter must hold proof of export — French doctrine and BOI guidance require physical departure within a three-month window from the sale/dispatch date unless a longer transport chain is documented; (2) ancillary services directly linked to those exports (transport, loading, brokerage, commission) under Article 262-I-1° 4°; (3) B2B services and software/intangible supplies to customers established outside the EU, which are placed outside France under the recipient-location rule of Article 259-A CGI where the non-EU establishment is evidenced and actual use occurs abroad; and (4) certain supplies to international organisations, embassies and international means of transport. For grid-tie solar inverters (ISIC 2790 / HS 8504.40), the zero-rating claim must be supported by customs exit validation, transport documents and non-EU recipient evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — Déclaration Unique d'Exportation (DAU) with the valid EU Movement Reference Number (MRN) issued and discharged by French customs in DELTA/Douane; the exit confirmation is the principal legal proof of export.

Transport and goods-handover evidence: signed bill of lading, sea waybill, air waybill or CIM rail consignment note showing final discharge outside the EU, container/seal numbers, modes of transport and dates; an attestation de prise en charge (AVT) issued by a customs-approved transporter may supplement missing waybills.

Original numbered commercial invoice stating INCOTERMS (EXW, FCA, CPT, CIF, etc.), payment terms, 0% TVA annotation, buyer's full identity and the technical description of the solar inverters/microinverters.

Packing list with serial numbers, package counts, gross/net weights and HS classification (8504.40), together with any applicable EUR.1/certificate of origin and CE/conformity documentation (e.g., EN 50549-1, NF C 73-311) demonstrating lawful production and supporting the commercial reality of the shipment.

Bank and FX remittance evidence: SWIFT MT103/MT202 credit advice or an official French bank attestation evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the non-EU buyer through the agreed payment rails (documentary letter of credit or wire transfer).

For services or software bundled with the inverters: contracts, delivery/installation reports and the customer's non-EU tax registration or establishment certificate (valid CRN, VAT registration outside the EU or equivalent), together with proof of actual use outside France.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French customs and the DGFiP treat export zero-rating as a high-risk claim. If the substantiation bundle is incomplete at the time of the VAT return or at audit, DGFiP reassesses the turnover at 20% TVA and reverses any refund. Reassessment rights generally run for three years after the year the VAT became due (Article L.176 LPF), extended to ten years for undisclosed/hidden activity or serious tax evasion. Applied charges include late-payment interest under Article 1727 CGI (0.20% per month), a 40% bad-faith penalty and an 80% fraudulent-manoeuvres penalty under Article 1729 CGI, plus specific e-invoicing and filing penalties under Articles 1728 and 1737 CGI. Retrospective clawbacks are automatic where the customer or an intermediary in the export chain did not in fact move goods outside the EU; sham export chains trigger the abuse-of-right procedure (80%-100%) and criminal referral under Articles 1741 and 1743 CGI (prison sanctions and fines up to EUR 500,000), joint and several liability of the gérant/directors under Article L.267 LPF, and possible co-assessment of the non-EU buyer where the parties knew or should have known of the fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) in conjunction with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) under the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Dépôt des Comptes Annuels) including balance sheet, income statement, notes, and statutory management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve accounts within six months of fiscal-year end; approved accounts must be filed with the Greffe within one month after approval (for 31 December year-end: approve by 30 June, file by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 9,000 for non-filing; court-ordered injunctive penalty (astreinte) up to EUR 310 per day; repeated non-filing over consecutive years may lead to judicial strike-off (radiation) from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Income Tax Return (Déclaration de Résultats et Liasse Fiscale n°2065)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year fiscal year: due by the second business day after 1 May (typically 3 May); for non-calendar fiscal year: due within three months of fiscal-year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of tax due; penalty increases to 40% if not filed within 30 days of a formal demand (mise en demeure), and to 80% for deliberate failure after enforcement; plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.2%.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) is mandatory for a SARL when it exceeds two of three thresholds: total assets greater than EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excluding VAT greater than EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees greater than 50. Auditors are also required for controlled entities in a group irrespective of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général – PCG) under ANC Regulation 2018-09 and the Code de Commerce; IFRS applies only to consolidated financial statements of listed entities or if required by group consolidation rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation is required under French law; beneficial-ownership declarations (déclarations des bénéficiaires effectifs) are filed upon incorporation and any modification, including the registration of share transfers, must be filed with the RCS within 30 days. The declaration discloses every direct or indirect owner of more than 25% of capital or voting rights, or senior managers when no shareholder reaches that threshold.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders' Decisions and Minutes (Registre des décisions et procès-verbaux)
Register of Share Movements (Registre des mouvements de titres)
Beneficial Ownership Register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% on first €42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs; R&D tax credit up to 30% of eligible expenses

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Déclaration de résultat via Portail des Entreprises (impots.gouv.fr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15th day of the 4th month after fiscal year-end (e.g. 15 April for calendar year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-sourced income; non-residents file for French branch or permanent establishment
Deductible expenses including arm's length related party costs

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 0.75% of tax due per month of delay, minimum €50, maximum 10% of tax due

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC form with tax residence certificate and beneficial ownership declaration to French tax authorities
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 5% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under most DTAs; Interest: 25% statutory, 0% under most DTAs if arm's length debt

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Applicable under French ESR rules to holding and IP holding companies; requires real economic activities and decision-making in France

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fraudulent understatement of taxable profits or false declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Up to 5 years imprisonment and fines up to 500% of evaded tax (minimum €500,000 in aggravated cases)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; directors face personal criminal liability, restitution orders, and possible imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a company without sufficient substance, employees, or decision-making in France
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of income, denial of tax deductions, penalties up to €75,000 or 10% of turnover
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for management fraud; potential criminal sanctions and disqualification

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct KYC, monitor transactions, or report suspicious activities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million and criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable; possible prison terms and civil liabilities
